Jacob Grimm, Wilhelm Grimm, Household Tales, translated by Margaret Hunt.
Standard Ebooks edition: https://standardebooks.org/ebooks/jacob-grimm_wilhelm-grimm/household-tales/margaret-hunt

People whose words are in the text, and their death years:
- Jacob Grimm, the author, died 1863 (Wikidata Q6701). Citizenship: Electorate of Hesse, Kingdom of Prussia.
- Wilhelm Grimm, the author, died 1859 (Wikidata Q6714). Citizenship: Landgraviate of Hesse-Kassel, Kingdom of Prussia.
- Margaret Hunt, the translator, died 1912 (Wikidata Q6759824). Citizenship: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Ireland.

First publication of the text used: 1857 (SE colophon: 'Household Tales was published in 1857 by Jacob Grimm and Wilhelm Grimm. It was translated from German in 1884 by Margaret Hunt.')

Why this is public domain:
- United States: works published before 1931 are in the public domain in the United States. The colophon dates the original to 1857 and the translation to 1884. The edition's rights statement (quoted below) says the same.
- Country of origin: the original German text (Germany) has a term of life plus 70 years. The last author of the original to die is Jacob Grimm, in 1863, so the original is public domain in Germany from 1 January 1934. The translation's country is not stated. The possible countries are the United Kingdom, Ireland, the United States, Canada, Australia, New Zealand, India and South Africa. Each has a term of life plus 70 years or less for these deaths. The last person to die among the people whose words are in the text is Margaret Hunt, in 1912, so the translation is public domain in each of them by 1 January 1983.

The edition's own statement of rights (from the repository's content.opf):
"The source text and artwork in this ebook are believed to be in the United States public domain; that is, they are believed to be free of copyright restrictions in the United States. They may still be copyrighted in other countries, so users located outside of the United States must check their local laws before using this ebook. The creators of, and contributors to, this ebook dedicate their contributions to the worldwide public domain via the terms in the [CC0 1.0 Universal Public Domain Dedication](https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/zero/1.0/)."

Sources of these facts:

- Wikidata Q6701 (Jacob Grimm), death year 1863
- Wikidata Q6714 (Wilhelm Grimm), death year 1859
